newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taipei gives cautious welcome to HK office--paper.
newsitem.headline: Taipei gives cautious welcome to HK office--paper.

text.p: Taiwan will allow Hong Kong to set up a Taipei office after the British colony reverts to rule under communist China, the island's arch rival, a newspaper said on Monday.

Taipei nevertheless cautioned that the handover of Hong Kong, main conduit for Taiwan's huge "indirect" investments in China, would increase Beijing's power to squeeze Taiwan politically, the United Daily News said.

"We will allow the Hong Kong government to set up a representative office in Taiwan...(it) is likely to want to do that," the newspaper quoted William Li, who oversees Hong Kong matters at the cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council, as saying.
"But after July 1 communist China will have more chips to play against Taiwan. If we do not have some sense of forewarning, then we are being too optimistic," Li said.
Some commentators have warned that Beijing was pursuing a strategy of luring Nationalist-ruled Taiwan into economic dependency on the mainland in a scheme to rein in the estranged island.
Beijing has considered Taiwan a renegade province since the two split after a civil war in 1949.

Hong Kong is the main transit point for some US$30 billion worth of investment projects that Taiwan businesses have poured into the mainland since cross-strait political tensions began to thaw in the 1980s. The sides still have no official ties.
Li was quoted as saying he expected Hong Kong and Taiwan to continue their current exchanges after the July 1 handover.
"Future travel and economic links between the people of Taiwan and Hong Kong will not change," Li said.
Taiwan and Hong Kong recently signed an 11th-hour agreement to allow ships to sail into each other's harbours, avoiding a sovereignty problem by agreeing that ships would enter port flying no flags.
Taiwan has adopted laws that regard Hong Kong as a special administrative zone in order to circumvent Taipei's longstanding ban on direct links with communist China.
